papers.title: Mobile-Enabled Pest Prediction in Sub-Saharan Africa: An Empirical Review of SMS and Mobile Platforms Bridging Traditional Farming Knowledge and Digital Early Warning Systems
papers.authors: Kosgey Festus Kipchirchir, Alice Nambiro
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Food security in Sub-Saharan Africa is threatened by a number of agricultural pests including the fall armyworm, desert locusts and stem borers. Typical pest monitoring, mostly conducted by manual scouting and late reporting, can inhibit prompt early warning and response. This paper presents a systematic review of the empirical evidence on SMS platforms, mobile applications and mobile based pest prediction systems with a focus on incorporating indigenous ecological knowledge. Using the thematic synthesis approach and supported by the Technology Acceptance Model, Diffusion of Innovation Theory and Information Systems Success Model, 54 peer-reviewed articles, institutional reports and conference papers were reviewed between 2018 and 2026. The results show that mobile platforms increase the timeliness and geographical scope of pest data collection and dissemination. By combining climatic, vegetation and historical pest information, machine-learning models can help improve accuracy over local conditions. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.authors: Alexandre Bout, Sylvie Warot, Lily Cesari, Rachid Hamidi, Claire Caravel
papers.abstract: Stink bugs (Hemiptera Pentatomidae) are major agricultural pests worldwide, including both native and invasive species. In France, for instance, Halyomorpha halys has rapidly expanded its range, affecting key crops such as hazelnuts, apples, and vegetables. Meanwhile, several native, polyphagous species - Nezara viridula, Palomena prasina and, to a lesser extent, Graphosoma italicum - are re-emerging and impacting diverse crops because of changes in agricultural practices and climatic conditions. Egg parasitoids represent promising biological control agents for these pests, be it through conservation, augmentation or introduction biological control. However, their actual potential is not precisely documented due to a lack of ambitious surveys and possible taxonomic issues. This study aims to address this gap by compiling results obtained from various of egg parasitism surveys of Pentatomidae in France and implementing a large-scale DNA Barcoding approach (2000 individuals) for the emerged parasitoids. papers.abstract: Abstract: Long COVID has emerged as a continuing public health challenge, with symptoms such as fatigue, cognitive slowing and shortness of breath affecting many people well after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review synthesizes evidence on prevalence, symptom, risk determinants, health utilization, and the wider social and economic effects of Long COVID, emphasizing prevention and health system preparedness. The analysis highlights differences across regions and population groups, rising pressure on rehabilitation services and notable consequences for employment, education and mental health. The study looks at fairness in resource distribution within overburdened health systems, equity in care access, and the protection of vulnerable groups in research and policy responses from an ethical standpoint. We underline the importance of harmonized diagnostic criteria, inclusive and representative research, and equitable access to chronic care services. We also set out priority policy actions to support earlier identification, team-based models of care and coordinated national strategies. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). We investigated prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted lipid-shelled perfluorocarbon nanobubbles (PSMA-NBs) in an orthotopic rabbit model using a clinical contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) system. We implanted PSMA-positive PC3pip-GFP tumors into the prostates of immunosuppressed New Zealand White rabbits and performed transabdominal imaging with PSMA-NBs, MBs, and Plain-NBs using identical protocols. To address tumor heterogeneity and ultrasound boundary ambiguity, regions of interest were defined from baseline B-mode images and segmented into the tumor core, rim, and a peritumoral area. papers.abstract: This study examined the effect of microfinance services on the performance of smallholder rice farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study described the socio-economic characteristics of the respondents, examined the effect of microfinance services on farmers' performance, and identified the constraints faced in accessing credit from microfinance banks. A multi-stage sampling technique was employed to select 384 smallholder rice farmers for the study. Primary data were collected using questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The results showed that the respondents were predominantly male (76.0%) and married (78.4%), with a mean age of 44 years, mean farm size of 2.24 ha, mean household size of 7 persons, and mean annual farm income of ₦1,087,650. The double-log model was selected as the lead equation based on its superior econometric properties (R² = 0.781, Adjusted R² = 0.777, F = 265.71, p < 0.01). papers.title: Notes on the Parasitoids of the Sugarcane Crown Mealybug Phenacoccus saccharifolii (Hemiptera: Pseudococcidae) in Tamil Nadu, India
papers.authors: Janakiraman Poorani, Ramalingam Thanigairaj
papers.abstract: Phenacoccus saccharifolii (Green) (Hemiptera: Pseudococcidae), commonly known as the sugarcane crown mealybug, has become a major pest of concern in recent years in the sugarcane growing areas of Tamil Nadu state, India. It is found either alone or in association with other sugarcane feeding mealybugs, particularly Dysmicoccus carens Williams, and the sugarcane aphid, Melanaphis sacchari (Zehntner) (Hemiptera: Aphididae). Recent publications on the crown mealybug, after it became a serious pest in southern India, provided only limited, and mostly erroneous, information on its parasitoids. In field surveys conducted during 2022-24 in Karur District, Tamil Nadu, we found Leptomastix sylvae Noyes & Hayat (Hymenoptera: Encyrtidae) to be a primary parasitoid of Ph. saccharifolii along with two hyperparasitoids, Promuscidea unfasciativentris Girault (Hymenoptera: Pirenidae) and Chartocerus sp. (Hymenoptera: Signiphoridae). Aenasius hayati Manickavasagam (Hymenoptera: Encyrtidae) was found as a parasitoid of D. carens for the first time. Brief illustrated notes on these parasitoids are provided, along with comments on the identities of the parasitoids recorded in recent publications.

Disease and insect scores were recorded before spraying and 14 days after treatment. Vegetative and biochemical parameters were assessed two weeks after treatment. papers.abstract: Trogoderma granarium Everts is a prevalent and devastating postharvest pest affecting stored wheat grains and various other stored commodities. The larvae's voracious feeding activity severely deteriorates wheat quality and quantity in warehouses. Traditional chemical controls, when used excessively, negatively affect the environment and food sources and encourage resistance. To address these challenges, we investigated an eco-friendly method for biosynthesizing magnesium oxide nanoparticles (MgO-NPs) using the aqueous extract of Artemisia herba-alba aerial parts, aiming for insecticidal application against T. granarium. The biosynthesized MgO-NPs were characterized through a qualitative assessment of color change, UV-visible spectrophotometer (UV/Vis), Energy-Dispersive X-ray analysis spectrometer (EDX), X-ray diffraction patterns (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). papers.title: Seasonal Population Dynamics of Major Sucking Pests of Chilli under Different Weather Conditions in Southern Karnataka, India
papers.authors: Gaurav Vinod Rao Sadafale, Prajwal Gowda M. A., Lavanya Narayan, Hanamantappa Meti, Gurulingappa Nagappa Sajjan
papers.abstract: A single year field investigation was conducted at Mandya, Karnataka during August-December 2023 (Rabi) and January-April 2024 (Summer) to evaluate the seasonal population dynamics of major sucking pests of chilli and their relationship with weather parameters. Distinct seasonal variations in pest incidence governed by abiotic factors were observed. During 2023, pest populations initiated from the 44th SMW and peaked in December, with Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood recording 10.25 thrips per three leaves, followed by Bemisia tabaci Gennadius (9.46), Amrasca biguttula biguttula Ishida (7.45), and Polyphagotarsonemus latus (Banks) (9.11). In Summer, higher pest incidence was observed, with S. dorsalis attaining a peak of 12.15 per three leaves (19th SMW), while B. tabaci (7.86), A. biguttula biguttula (7.34), and P. latus (8.45) showed sustained incidence. papers.abstract: Environmental contamination of freshwater habitats is increasingly recognized as a factor influencing the ecology of disease vectors. In this study, we used life table-based analyses to examine the effects of three concentrations of sodium dodecylbenzene sulfonate, a detergent/surfactant pollutant (0, 1.5, and 8.5 ppm), on the survival, reproductive output, and transmission potential of Anopheles stephensi under laboratory conditions. Population growth parameters including intrinsic rate of increase ( r m ), finite rate of increase ( λ ), and net reproductive rate ( R 0 ) exhibited treatment-dependent variations, with the 1.5 ppm group generally showing reduced reproductive output, whereas the 8.5 ppm group maintained rates comparable to the control group. Life history traits, including preadult and adult longevity, fecundity, and female-to-male ratios, revealed distinct patterns across treatments, highlighting potential sex-specific sensitivities. papers.title: Impulsive Release Strategies for Wolbachia-Infected Mosquitoes Under Temperature-Induced Infection Loss
papers.authors: J Alves, Christian E. Schaerer, Cláudia P. Ferreira
papers.abstract: The release of Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes is a promising strategy for controlling Aedes aegypti populations, although high-temperature exposure may temporarily reduce infection levels and compromise long-term persistence. We propose a population-dynamics model based on impulsive differential equations that incorporates cytoplasmic incompatibility, periodic mosquito releases, and temperature-driven infection loss. Analytical results establish fundamental qualitative properties of the continuous and impulsive models, derive conditions for the existence and stability of periodic solutions, and provide an explicit release threshold for the successful establishment and long-term persistence of the infected population. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical results and compare the performance of the wMelPop, wMel, and wAlbB strains under different thermal scenarios, highlighting the influence of strain-specific fitness costs and thermal tolerance. Additional simulations investigate temperature-dependent demographic variation and imperfect maternal transmission, extending the analysis beyond the assumptions of the analytical framework. papers.abstract: Introduction Malaria remains a significant public health challenge in tropical regions. The disease is driven by multiple Anopheles vector species with varied ecological and behavioral traits. In transitional zones like the forested Pouth-Kelle community, detailed knowledge of vector dynamics and disease transmission remains limited. This study aimed to characterize local Anopheles species composition, biting behavior, and malaria transmission indicators to guide control strategies. Morphological and molecular techniques were used for species identification. Entomological indicators were assessed, and an ELISA assay was conducted to detect Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite proteins in order to determine infection rate. Concurrently, residents were screened for malaria by microscopy. Statistical analysis examined the relationship between infection rate, age, and sex. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Today, soil pollution with heavy metals and petroleum compounds is one of the main environmental problems. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. papers.title: Biochemical Studies on Gamma Radiation Effects in Honey Bee (Apis mellifera) Workers
papers.authors: Mohamed M. Abdel-Monsef, Sameh G. Sawires, Doaa A. Darwish
papers.abstract: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) are highly sensitive to environmental stressors, including gamma radiation. We evaluated the biochemical responses of adult worker bees to graded gamma-irradiation doses (20, 30, 40 and 50 rad). Total soluble protein content and the activities of key enzymes; superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), glutathione S-transferase (GST), malate dehydrogenase (MDH), acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and acid phosphatase (ACP) were measured, and native PAGE was used to assess protein and enzyme profiles. Results showed a clear biphasic response: at the low dose (20 rad), total protein increased to 3.45 mg/mL (compared to 1.32 mg/mL in controls), and all enzyme activities were elevated, with SOD and CAT showing the largest increases (+1.24- and +1.19-fold, respectively), indicating an adaptive, radio-hormetic response. At intermediate doses (30-40 rad), protein levels and enzymatic activities progressively declined, and at the highest dose (50 rad), total protein (1.33 mg/mL) and enzyme activities approached or fell below control levels, reflecting oxidative damage and reduced metabolic and neurophysiological function. papers.authors: Nina Bziuk, Matthias Cambeis, Karolin Pohl, Joseph Nesme, Søren Johannes Sørensen
papers.abstract: Abstract Background and aims Microbial inoculants are increasingly recognized for enhancing crop productivity and sustainable agriculture. We assessed the rhizosphere competence of Ensifer meliloti Rm2011 in different barley genotypes following repeated inoculation in three growing seasons, tracking its establishment and influence on the indigenous rhizosphere prokaryotic communities. We aimed to understand how consistent field application affects prokaryotic dynamics and whether environmental conditions or plant genotype modulate its establishment within the rhizosphere community. Methods Three-year field trials evaluated the establishment of E. meliloti Rm2011 in barley rhizosphere and its impact on the prokaryotic community. Rhizosphere samples were collected at several time points throughout the vegetation period and analyzed using colony-forming units and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to further evaluate the effects of barley genotype and environmental conditions. papers.authors: Meenakshi Jeena, Gaurav Kumar, Bharti Goyal, Suman Lata, Lipun Kumar Pradhan
papers.abstract: Introduction Extensive and long-term insecticide use has led to the development of resistance in mosquito vectors, underscoring the need for novel insecticidal molecules and integrated, multifaceted strategies that simultaneously target both the vector and the parasite. In line with this, we evaluated the potential of a lipophilic drug triclosan, as a contact-mediated inhibitor to block the development of Plasmodium parasite within the malaria vector, Anopheles stephensi . Methods Molecular docking and simulations identified the potential of triclosan to interact with the ookinete surface proteins of the Plasmodium species. Intrinsic toxicity of triclosan was first established on both larval and adult stages of laboratory reared An. stephensi through oral feeding and contact exposure (topical application and bottle bio-assay) in terms of survival and/or fecundity and egg hatchability. papers.authors: Fahimeh Talebzadeh, Reza Raoofian, Hadi Babaei, Kamal Azam, Seyed Ehsan Mousavi
papers.abstract: Hematophagous insects found at crime scenes can be forensically useful, as human DNA from their blood meals may help identify suspects or victims. This study evaluates the use of two commercial STR kits, IG_17Plex (17-loci) and IG_GrandPlex (28-loci), to obtain human short tandem repeat (STR) profiles from blood-fed Culex pipiens , Anopheles stephensi , and Phlebotomus papatasi . Both kits were tested for amplification reliability and compared for performance. The effect of post-feeding time was assessed by euthanizing insects at 12-h intervals up to 72 h. We also tested mixed blood meals in both An. stephensi and Cx. pipiens , finding comparable results between the two species. Additionally, we compared four preservation methods, ethanol immersion (with or without cuticle) and freezing (with or without cuticle), on DNA integrity in blood-fed An. stephensi . STR kits consistently amplified complete profiles from blood-fed mosquitoes, but sand flies yielded only partial profiles. papers.title: Conservation-oriented comparison of non-contact robotic survey systems for immovable cultural heritage in constrained environments
papers.authors: Wei Zhou, Yanmin Xue, Shuang Wang, Kai Qi, Zhuoya Zhang
papers.abstract: Non-contact survey of immovable cultural heritage in complex and constrained environments faces challenges from limited accessibility, structural occlusion, GNSS denial, fragile materials, and strict deployment requirements. This review synthesizes evidence on aerial robots, ground mobile robots, special-purpose systems, including cable-driven robots and manipulators, and heterogeneous collaborative systems. Existing studies remain fragmented across individual platforms, algorithms, and application scenarios, limiting conservation-oriented cross-platform comparison. Through systematic literature screening, evidence-role classification, cross-platform coding, and technology-readiness assessment, platforms are evaluated in terms of conservation safety, task effectiveness, and deployment maturity. Results show that suitability depends on material sensitivity, spatial configuration, survey requirements, and deployment conditions. papers.authors: Jian Zhao, Siyu Zhu, Yulong Li, Mi Zhang, Fangyuan Xu
papers.abstract: Abstract Poplar canker threatens the health and productivity of poplar plantations, but its association with the rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly resolved. We profiled bacterial 16 S V3-V4 and fungal ITS1 communities in root-zone soils from asymptomatic and canker-symptomatic Populus talassica at Qitai, Nileke, and Dabancheng, with three independent composite samples per site-by-status group. Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA detected effects of sampling site, disease status, and their interaction on bacterial and fungal community dissimilarity. Location-based dispersion analyses further indicated that these differences were driven by changes in community composition rather than solely by shifts in group centroids. While no overall differences in Shannon alpha diversity were observed between asymptomatic and canker-symptomatic trees after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, site-level differences were detected.
